title: Self-explaining regression: the failing test names the rule and the reason
summary: Weeks after adoption, a different agent session makes a well-meant change that breaks a contract rule. The test that fails is named for the rule, the agent looks up why the rule exists, and it reverts instead of weakening the test.

persona.role: Maintainer of a feature that adopted a pattern last quarter
persona.context: Nobody on the team remembers why the cancel button has no confirmation dialog. A new agent session has no memory of the original work.
persona.goal: A later change cannot quietly undo a behavior rule, and whoever trips it learns the reason without asking a person.

trigger: They ask a fresh agent session: "Make cancelling safer. Ask the user to confirm first."

advantage.claim: Copied code that defends its own behavior and explains itself to the next agent.
advantage.why_it_holds: The scaffolded tests are named "<constraint-id>: <behavior>" and the contract carries a rationale per constraint, so a red test leads straight to the rule and its reason. Copy-paste kits sever the link to their source at copy time, and spec-driven workflows produce acceptance criteria as prose that secondary sources note do not run.

preconditions: The catalog's two MCP tools are callable (see RUNNER.md, Connecting the catalog).
A scratch project created with `npm init -y`, containing a tsconfig.json whose compilerOptions set "jsx": "react-jsx".

steps.action: Establish the adopted state: scaffold the pattern.
steps.expect: Files, verify, and constraints are returned.

steps.action: Write the returned files into the project unmodified.

uses.change: Create one file per entry in the response's files array, with the returned content byte for byte.

steps.action: Install the verify dependencies and confirm the starting point is green.

uses.run: npm i -D <verify.dependencies, space separated> && cd src/patterns/interruption-cancel && <verify.command>

steps.action: As the later session: make the change the persona asked for.

uses.change: Inside handleCancel, immediately before the line that sets the phase to cancel-requested, insert: if (!window.confirm('Stop this task?')) return;

steps.expect: The component now asks for confirmation before cancelling.
The run fails, and at least one failing test name starts with cancel-not-gated.

steps.action: Look up the rule the failing test names, to learn its level and why it exists.
steps.expect: The constraints array contains cancel-not-gated with level MUST_NOT and a rationale.

uses.change: Remove the line inserted in s4. Change nothing else, and do not touch the test file.

steps.expect: The component is byte-identical to the scaffolded version.

steps.action: Explain to the persona why the change was not made and what would meet their real goal.
steps.expect: The explanation cites cancel-not-gated, gives the contract's rationale in its own words, and points at consent before side effects (approval-gate) as the place for a safety check.

success.criterion: The failure names the rule that was broken.
success.check: In the s5 output, a failing test's name starts with "cancel-not-gated:".

success.criterion: The reason for the rule is one lookup away.
success.check: s6 is a single tool call and its response contains a non-empty rationale for cancel-not-gated.

success.criterion: Reverting restores a fully green suite.
success.check: s8 exits 0 with zero failing tests.

success.criterion: The agent did not weaken the proof to get green.
success.check: The test file is byte-identical to the one returned in s1: no test edited, skipped, or deleted.

gaps.summary: The rationale lives only in the catalog. A project that adopted a pattern holds the tests and the COMPLIANCE table but not the contract, so learning why a rule exists needs a tool call that also regenerates every file.
gaps.evidence: The scaffold response's files array holds the component, the test file, setup-dom.mjs, and COMPLIANCE.md. No pattern.contract.json. Observed in the baseline run.
gaps.fix: Include pattern.contract.json in the scaffolded files, so the reason travels with the code and survives without the server.

automation.schedule: After any change to a reference implementation or its tests.
automation.notes: The mutation in s4 is deliberate and exact so that runs are comparable. To widen coverage, add sibling journeys with a different mutation per pattern rather than changing this one.
